events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.33 (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered ride (F6: metered $49.37), and one off-route segment exists: 09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, +3.07 km [F3][RD-1]. Under RD-1 any unexplained deviation is a non-exempt detour; the driver's post-trip statement "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is a claim, not rider consent [F10][RD-5].

RD-4 does not excuse the segment: the traffic records show only speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, i.e. free-flowing conditions, and no incident near the route during the trip window [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. Band 5 is nowhere near the band 1–2 congestion threshold, and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment [RD-4].

RD-5 is not satisfied either. The complete chat record contains only the rider's pickup message and the driver's arrival message, both before pickup, at 09:04 and 09:05; neither says anything about the route to Changi [F7][F8][F9]. The rider therefore sent no agreement before the segment began at 09:24 [RD-5]. The driver's assertion of GPS rerouting appears only in his own statement, which is not consent [F10][RD-5]. For the same reason RD-3 does not apply: no rider message named any stop or place in this segment, and no stop is measured in it [F7][F8][RD-3].

On the metered fare, only the extra distance of the non-exempt segment is refundable: $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.4101/km [F6][RD-2]. 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290, rounded to $4.33 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. The unallocated corridor jitter is not refunded [RD-2].

RD-6 does not attach an account action: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days, but zero of them involve route, so route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and this case does not make him "repeated" for route deviation [F16][RD-6]. The 1.0× surge and no discount are consistent with the total (base $3.90 + distance $34.42 + time $9.58 + platform $1.47 = $49.37), so no FARE-1 item is refundable [F5][F6][FARE-1].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We've finished reviewing your ride to Changi. We're refunding you $4.33 as a Ryde voucher. The trip was metered, and while part of the route was a normal detour, one stretch in the middle — about 3 km beyond the best route — wasn't explained or agreed to before it happened, and the roads were free-flowing at the time, so that part is on us. Only that extra distance is refunded. The voucher goes to your Ryde account, and there's nothing else you need to do. Your account isn't affected.

DRIVER: We've reviewed the route dispute on this metered trip. Outcome: a $4.33 partial refund to the rider, paid as a Ryde voucher, covering roughly 3 km of extra distance on one segment. What decided it: the deviation wasn't agreed with the rider beforehand, and traffic at the time was free-flowing, so the segment wasn't exempt. Getting a reroute from your GPS doesn't count as rider agreement. No account flag or action is being taken — you have no prior upheld route disputes, so this isn't treated as repeated. You don't need to do anything; the voucher is issued by Ryde and doesn't come out of your earnings.
